title: Wednesday, September 16, 2026

headline.title: The decision is 93% priced. The dot plot is not. The Fed announces at 1:00 CT with futures at roughly 93% for a 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% — the first increase since July 2023 — and Chair Warsh takes the podium at 1:30 CT with a fresh set of dots. That is where the actual information is. The June dot plot penciled in one more hike for 2026; futures are leaning toward two by year-end. The decision itself resolves nothing because everyone already holds it. The gap between one dot and two is the trade.
headline.summary: A style note that matters more than usual: Warsh favors minimalist communication. Expect fewer promises and more data-dependence, which means the bond market will be left to do its own interpreting — and the bond market is already at a level it has not seen in nearly two decades. The 10-year touched 5.045% intraday Tuesday, its highest since 2007, before settling right on the 5% line. Ahead of all of it, August retail sales land at 7:30 CT, seen rebounding about +0.9% after July's −0.6% — the biggest monthly drop in over a year. BofA card data still shows spending up 4.5% year-over-year, so the consumer read is genuinely open rather than pre-written.

overview:
Futures are modestly green and the semis are leading again for a third straight session of this tug-of-war. INTC +3.50%, LRCX +2.02%, ARM +1.88%, AMD +1.75%, DELL +1.45%. The AI-slowdown story has now had its panic (Monday), its rebuttal (Tuesday, via Huang) and its third day of quiet grinding — the complex is no longer trading the essay, it is trading the Fed like everything else.

The two-day damage was elsewhere, and it came from Washington. The CLARITY Act procedural vote failed in the Senate, Bitcoin slid into the $76,800 range and is near $75k this morning, and the crypto complex wore it in full: COIN −7.1%, CRCL −9.1%, HOOD −3.7% on Tuesday. That was the cleanest single-catalyst move of the session and it had nothing to do with AI or the Fed.

Watch the rotation inside this morning's tape, because it is the one that reads as pre-positioning. GLD is +1.16% while USO is −1.69% — gold bid and crude giving back, the first time this week that pairing has gone this direction. Oil is pausing but holding above $100 after WTI settled near $104 (+2.6%) and Brent near $108 (+2.1%) Tuesday on the Saudi pipeline shutdown and continued Houthi attacks. Freight is the morning's disaster: JBHT −10.46%, the board's biggest down-mover, the morning after its own conference appearance, with fellow trucker KNX −4.4% carrying a bearish kicker beside it. A double-digit break in a transport bellwether on a conference day is a demand signal worth more attention than it will get today.

One structural note worth holding onto before the sequence: Friday is triple witching, two sessions after a live decision, which is why this morning's sheet weights CRM 20% weeklies / 80% next week rather than buying the cheap expiry. Contracts dated 09/18 have to survive the most mechanical session of the quarter to pay.

Today's sequence: retail sales 7:30 CT, crude inventories 9:30 CT, the decision 1:00 CT, Warsh 1:30 CT. OSCR's Investor Day runs at 8:00 CT and it is +1.63% into it; ON Semiconductor's Analyst Day lands the same day with the stock +1.50%; CRM's Investor & Analyst Session is 3:00 CT, at the bell; and LEN reports after the close — a homebuilder printing hours after a rate hike with mortgage rates north of 7%, Street near $1.30 and expected lower year-over-year.

watchlist.em_label: MARKS VS TUESDAY 9/15 CLOSE — DECISION DAY, DOT PLOT AT 1:00 CT

setups: The only unpriced thing on the calendar

93% of the market already owns the hike. A 25bp move to 3.75–4.00% is not information; it is confirmation. The information is the dots. June's plot penciled one more 2026 hike. Futures are positioned for two by year-end. If the new plot shows one, the front end has to unwind a hike it is carrying; if it shows two or more, the 10-year at 5% gets a fresh reason to go higher. And Warsh's minimalist style makes the dots louder, not quieter — a chair who declines to guide leaves the plot as the only forward signal in the room. The risk: a hawkish dot plot into a 10-year that already tagged its highest level since 2007 is the combination that breaks the equity calm, and the calm is what everything above is priced on.
The last real data before the decision

July fell −0.6%, the biggest monthly drop in over a year, and consensus looks for a +0.9% rebound. The reason this is genuinely open rather than pre-written: BofA card data still shows spending up 4.5% year-over-year, which does not square with a consumer that fell off a cliff in July. A hot print hands Warsh cover for a hawkish plot; a soft one makes the second dot much harder to justify — and it lands five and a half hours before the decision, so the tape gets to reprice twice. Watch the control group rather than the headline.
The event, then the decision, on the same clock

Oscar Health presents long-term financial targets an hour before the open, then the Fed decides five hours later. Our own five-event study makes this the one to respect: OSCR's June 2024 Investor Day ran 2.15x average volume and a 2.16 ATR range — the most violent of the five — falling 12.19% from the open before closing +0.42% from it. The entire move was in the path. The tell is visible early: across all five events, volume in the first thirty minutes ordered the day's range almost perfectly. An Investor Day that does not bring volume does not bring movement. It closed Tuesday 32.44, down 4.05%, giving back the whole of Monday's gain before the event.

darkpool.note: Roughly $5B of S&P 500 tracker size printed after hours, all of it bid-side, the night before a near-certain rate hike. VOO $1.8B (bid) was the largest print on the whole board — the seventh straight session an S&P tracker has topped the tape — with IVV $1.7B (bid) and SPY $1.5B (bid) stacked behind it. That is index money repositioning into the event rather than an opinion about a single name, and the lean-not-verdict caveat applies twice over on index flow. In single names the mega-caps leaned the same way: NVDA, AMD, MSFT, AVGO and AAPL all printed at the bid. MU and PLTR took the ask side instead — and MU has now taken over the top of cumulative flow at $4.9B (mixed), ahead of NVDA $4.3B (bid) and META $3.1B (ask).
darkpool.right_note: The board is working both ends of the clock. Largest block: ICE $145C 09/18 at $26.8M, a floor call block expiring Friday on triple witching, two days after the decision — about as short-dated as size gets. Largest sweep: META $670C 01/21/28 at $4.6M, dated out to January 2028, on the same name carrying $3.1B of ask-side cumulative flow. One ticket pointed at Friday, one pointed at 2028.
